blocks.text: Advanced testing and debugging techniques help create reliable and efficient applications. They go beyond fixing obvious errors: they find hidden problems that may affect how a program works, improve performance and user satisfaction, and make future maintenance easier.

items: Unit testing: checks each small part of the program (topic Unit Testing).
Breakpoints and watches: pause the program and inspect its values (topic Using Breakpoints and Watches).
Exception handling: lets the program survive errors while it runs (topic Exception Handling).
Profiling and optimisation: find and speed up slow parts (topic 5.3).

blocks.prompt: Name two techniques this chapter uses to make programs more reliable, and what each does.
blocks.explanation: For example, unit testing checks that each function gives the expected output, and exception handling stops the program crashing when an error occurs at runtime. (Breakpoints with watches, and profiling, are also correct answers.)

items: Advanced techniques find hidden problems, not only obvious errors.
They improve reliability, performance and maintainability.
